 ORDER ************ [Order of the Court was made by D.KRISHNAKUMAR, J.] This Writ Petition has been filed as a Public Interest Litigation seeking for a direction to the respondents to take effective steps to protect the life of the Tamil Nadu Fishermen fishing in Arabic Ocean, Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal and Balk Bay by providing safety life jackets to the fishermen in Tamil Nadu at free of cost and for a consequential direction to the respondents to provide rehabilitation assistance to the fishermen who were affected by 'Cyclone Ockhi'.

3 2.A counter affidavit has been filed by the fifth respondent. The relevant portion of the counter affidavit is as under:
16.With reference to the averments made in para-17 of the affidavit , it is submitted that due to gusty winds and severe storm, fishing boats are advised to reach to the nearest fishing harbours of various coastal States for safe berthing. To attend their immediate need and to provide rehabilitation, 5 Senior level IAS officers were deputed by Tamil Nadu Government to Karnataka, Kerala, Gujarat, Maharashtra and L a k s h a d w e e p . I n o r d e r t o p r o v i d e n e c e s s a r y a s s i s t a n c e t o t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis fishermen landed at various states who had faced shortage of food materials and fuel for returning to their original berthing base in the afermath of cyclone Ockhi as weather conditions were improving, the Government had immediately sanctioned a sum of Rs.2.20 crore towards providing fuel to the fishing crafts berthed in other states to bring them back to home and also for providing financial assistance to meet out the ration expenses. In accordance with the Govt order, 205 boats with 1,568 fishermen were safely returned to their native places. Details furnished below:-

(Ms)No.111, Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries (FS3) Employment in Government Department, dated 31.05.2018 organization to any one of the permitting in the posts namely legal heir of the deceased / Anganwadi workers, Anganwadi missing fishermen due to OCKHI helpers, Nutritious Meal cyclone Organizers, Nutritious Meal cook, Nutritious Meal cook assistant and Village assistant.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  An amount of Rs.42,50,000/- has been sanctioned to provide livelihood assistance of Rs.5000/- per family to the families of fishermen who went missing due to OCKHI cyclone. 
 An amount of Rs.16.50 crore has been sanctioned towards Special livelihood assistance at Rs.5000/- per family to the fishermen families of Kanniyakumari district affected by the OCKHI Cyclone. A sum of Rs. 15.38 crore has been disbursed to 30,756 fishermen families of Kanniyakumari District.  An amount of Rs.2,20,95,800/- has been sanctioned towards providing diesel for bringing back the boats to home town and to meet ration expenses to the fishermen affected during OCKHI Cyclonic storm.  An amount of Rs.10 lakh has been given to 20 fishermen as medical relief assistance.  An amount of Rs.40.80 crore was released to 204 families of fishermen @ Rs.20 lakh per family, who died/missing due to OCKHI cyclone. 
 An amount of Rs.8.445 crore was sanctioned from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)
towards payment of relief assistance for the damages caused to fishing boats and fishing implements due to OCKHI cyclone. 
18.With reference to the averments made in para-20 of the affidavit , it is submitted that after the occurrence of OCKHI cyclone, a memorandum https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis has been Vetrikumaran vs The Principal Secretary on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25776244/
5 submitted to the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India by the Hon'ble Chief Minister, in which it has been proposed for supply of 1500 number of HF sets to the deep sea going fishing boats at a cost of Rs.
109.00 Crore. Further, the department of Fisheries has given following communication equipments to ensure safety and security of the fishermen in deep seas:
i) Distress Alert Transmitters ii) Wireless Communication Equipments iii) Communication Equipments iv) WebGIS based Mobile app THOONDIL v) Transponders in Mechanized fishing boats.
19.It is submitted that the Government of Tamil Nadu accords utmost priority for the safety and wellbeing of the fishermen of Tamil Nadu. This Government unequivocally enunciate the commitment for an all inclusive growth of Fisheries sector in the State to provide our fishermen fraternity the safety, security, enhanced livelihood opportunities, social security and quality of life for fishermen by pioneering in implementing multi various developmental and welfare schemes in fisheries and aquaculture sector. 
3.According to the learned Additional Government Pleader, the aforesaid counter affidavit itself clearly states that steps have been taken by the Government to protect the Tamil Nadu fishermen. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.Insofar as the second limb of the prayer is concerned, we would not go into that aspect of the matter as it is a matter of consideration by the Government. Therefore, we are not inclined to grant such relief to the petitioner. 
5.Accordingly, this Writ Petition stands dismissed. There shall be no order as to costs.

summary.facts:
This Writ Petition has been filed as a Public Interest Litigation seeking for a direction to the respondents to take effective steps to protect the life of the Tamil Nadu Fishermen fishing in Arabic Ocean, Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal and Balk Bay by providing safety life jackets to the fishermen in Tamil Nadu at free of cost and for a consequential direction to the respondents to provide rehabilitation assistance to the fishermen who were affected by 'Cyclone Ockhi'.
, it is submitted that due to gusty winds and severe storm, fishing boats are advised to reach to the nearest fishing harbours of various coastal States for safe berthing.
fishermen landed at various states who had faced shortage of food materials and fuel for returning to their original berthing base in the afermath of cyclone Ockhi as weather conditions were improving, the Government had immediately sanctioned a sum of Rs.2.20 crore towards providing fuel to the fishing crafts berthed in other states to bring them back to home and also for providing financial assistance to meet out the ration expenses.
In accordance with the Govt order, 205 boats with 1,568 fishermen were safely returned to their native places.
, it is submitted that the following relief and rehabilitation packages have been announced by the Government and are implemented to restore normal life of the fishermen who were affected by cyclone Ockhi:-

rehabilitation assistance 3. Hospitalized and under Rs.50,000/-
treatment 4.

 An amount of Rs.8.445 crore was sanctioned from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)
towards payment of relief assistance for the damages caused to fishing boats and fishing implements due to OCKHI cyclone.
is submitted that the Government of Tamil Nadu accords utmost priority for the safety and wellbeing of the fishermen of Tamil Nadu.
This Government unequivocally enunciate the commitment for an all inclusive growth of Fisheries sector in the State to provide our fishermen fraternity the safety, security, enhanced livelihood opportunities, social security and quality of life for fishermen by pioneering in implementing multi various developmental and welfare schemes in fisheries and aquaculture sector.
